budgets.label: critical path (package code in the entry chunk)
budgets.why: User-facing promise of the package, accepted by the owner on 2026-10-23 when the demo budget moved to 101.5 KB: the default configuration adds at most 1 KB to the critical path and the first MP4 loads at most 24 KB lazily. This row is the first half: the package code in the host entry chunk (the lazyProbe stub, ProbeError and the engine list), cut out of the entry chunk by its sourcemap. Vite's preload helper is not counted here, because every Vite app with a dynamic import already has it; the entry chunk row counts it. Design estimate 1.0 KB; measured 0.67 KB, and measured plus 10 percent rounded up to 0.5 KB is also 1.0 KB.

budgets.label: entry chunk with the preload helper
budgets.why: The whole host entry chunk: the package code of the critical path row, Vite's preload helper, which Vite adds to the entry chunk of any app with a dynamic import, and the one line of host code. The critical path row stays the package promise; this row also catches what the package makes Vite add next to its code, such as a longer preload dependency list per dynamic import. Measured 1.40 KB. The limit is the first measurement from the packed tarball plus 10 percent, rounded up to 0.5 KB.

budgets.label: first MP4 analysis, lazy total
budgets.why: User-facing promise of the package, accepted by the owner on 2026-10-23 when the demo budget moved to 101.5 KB: the default configuration adds at most 1 KB to the critical path and the first MP4 loads at most 24 KB lazily. This row is the second half: everything the first MP4 or MOV file loads lazily, which is the probe client, the own worker entry, the statistics chunk (requested in parallel with the parser) and the ISO BMFF parser. budgets.label: all own paths, lazy total

budgets.label: emitted lazy total (every file outside the entry chunk)
budgets.why: Every JavaScript file the build emits outside the entry chunk, fetched or not: the probe client with its compare and fallback chunks, the own worker with its chunks, and the main-thread copies of the parsers, the statistics, the sniffer and the worker runtime. The default flavor keeps them as an in-thread own for environments without a Worker global (SSR, Node) and for worker: 'inline'; a root analyze(), not imported here, always runs in the calling thread on the same copies. A browser with a Worker global never fetches them otherwise, so the lazy totals above leave them out. This row bounds what the package adds to the deploy and the CDN. Measured 72.20 KB. The limit is the first measurement from the packed tarball plus 10 percent, rounded up to 0.5 KB. Raised from 79.5 KB to 81 KB in 0.2.0, measured 80.43 KB, when the ffprobe frame rate estimate began to read the H.264 slice headers: the build emits that code twice, in the own worker and in the main-thread copy.
